opening_message:
Ticket 1: Terri Koch (employee ID E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E009.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Terri Koch (E009) is a full-time Engineer and requested admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist). So the maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Terri Koch (E009): contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training; never admin). Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read. Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing her as full-time; per Security DB she is a contractor.
reason: Terri Koch (E009) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is above the maximum under both possible interpretations: HR says she is full-time with role Engineer, and Engineer does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist), so the full-time max is write (admin not allowed). Security says she is a contractor with basic security training, making the contractor max read (write requires advanced training, never admin). Because the employee facts conflict, I apply the more restrictive, documented security record: contractor with basic training => max read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
